subject: SparkCart launch — traffic matrix & temporary quota increase request
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T08:14:00Z
Subject: SparkCart launch — traffic matrix & temporary quota increase request

Team — looping you in on a time-sensitive request from SparkCart. They plan to flip a new checkout feature during Prime week and expect an initial burst of inference traffic for cart-summarization and fraud-rerank calls. Summary below: 

- Ask: +3x per-minute quota for the SparkCart account for 48 hours (target window: 2027-04-10 00:00 UTC -> 2027-04-12 00:00 UTC) and a soft increase in concurrent requests for their dedicated routes.
- Forecast (attached): peak 18k gen tokens/min, sustained 6k tokens/min outside peak minutes.
- Why: real-time scoring + live user prompts for cart personalization; they will shift some traffic to a cached path after 12 hours but need runway.

Attached is their traffic workbook (sparkcart_launch_forecast_v1.xlsx) and a short SLA exception doc they asked us to sign. Key questions: 
1) Product: can we route their low-latency endpoint to a slightly higher-throughput (quantized) model without breaking integrations?
2) Infra (Neha): do we have capacity and an ops playbook to run a 48h quota bump? What telemetry/kill-switch do you need?
3) CS / Sales (Connor): what commitments are we comfortable making on fallbacks, and do we need a formal canary?

Can everyone reply with their constraints and a recommended plan by EOD so I can feed back to Lena.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-01T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkCart launch — traffic matrix & temporary quota increase request

On 2027-04-01 08:14, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — looping you in on a time-sensitive request from SparkCart.

Quick product note: A few clarifications so we avoid surprises during the bump: 
- Model variants: We can route their route to a 4-bit quantized variant of the same family which preserves output shape but has ~1.6x throughput improvement in our benchmarks. That should cover most of the token load without changing client integration.
- Latency: quantized path adds ~8-12ms p50 in our infra tests, p95 impact negligible for these request sizes. If SparkCart requires sub-100ms p95 we should keep them on the FP16 path with a lower batch size.
- Feature toggles: product can add a runtime flag to force the quantized model for the route; needs a week to stage + a canary (we have 72hr runway if we start now).

Actionable asks for Karthik: confirm whether SparkCart can tolerate the small p50 hit and whether their SDK pins model config. If they cannot, we need to pre-warm additional FP16 capacity which ups the cost.

-Marissa
Director, Product (Serving Runtime)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkCart launch — traffic matrix & temporary quota increase request

Karthik / team — looked at the attached workbook. High level: we can run a 48h quota uplift but with constraints and a pre-warm checklist. Notes: 

- Capacity: We have spare headroom in us-west-2 for the 4/10–4/12 window if we commit to the quantized variant Marissa suggested. If they insist on FP16 we need a minimum of 12 additional GPU-hours pre-allocated (will require a small reserved burst allocation and cost notify).
- Autoscaling policy: I'll provision a temporary policy with a hard cap and a 30% buffer. We need a manual kill-switch (ops-runbook) in case of runaway traffic. I will own the runbook during the bump window.
- Telemetry: require these metrics to be instrumented and pushed to the alerting channel: per-route tokens/min, per-route concurrent requests, error-rate, p50/p95 latency, and KV cache hit-rate. If error-rate > 2% sustained for 5m we roll back.
- Canary: recommend a 6-hour canary with 10% traffic for the quantized model starting 2027-04-10 00:00 UTC, then ramp to 100% over 2 hours (assuming nothing anomalous).

Attachments: I'll add a short ops checklist to the Drive link and the change request to our internal deployment board.

-Neha
Principal Infra PM
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkCart launch — traffic matrix & temporary quota increase request

Thanks — a few commercial/CS items: 

- Customer commitments: SparkCart asked for a documented fallback plan and a short SLO note. I can draft a one-page runbook (public-facing) that explains our fallback to reduced-throughput model + cache strategies and what to expect if we throttle. We should avoid contractual SLA changes for a temporary bump; instead offer a limited credit if we miss their stated throughput during the window.
- Legal / exceptions: The SLA-exception-request.docx looks standard; loop in Legal if they want anything beyond credits.
- Communication plan: I propose daily check-ins during the bump (8am/2pm UTC) and a single war-room Slack channel (I can create #sparkcart-launch). Who will own the channel? Ops needs to be primary.

I'll also push a short email template for the customer should we need to notify about rollback.

-Connor
Customer Success Manager
From: Lena Park <lena@sparkcart.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T16:23:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkCart launch — traffic matrix & temporary quota increase request

Hi Karthik — thanks for the quick internal sync. A few answers inline: 

> can SparkCart tolerate small p50 hit?
Yes — we validated the integration and can tolerate up to a 15ms increase on average. Prioritizing throughput over tiny p50s is fine for us.

> can you do a 6-hour canary then ramp?
Yes, that plan works. We'll start the canary with 10% of North America traffic.

We attached an updated forecast with hourly windows and a contact list for on-call engineers (sparkcart_launch_forecast_v1.xlsx). We prefer the war-room Slack channel to include our Ops lead (ops@sparkcart.com). Please confirm final timing by Friday so we can update internal runbooks.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Head of Engineering
SparkCart
